questions.question: A BI-RADS Category 0 assessment on a screening mammogram indicates:
choices: There is a definitely benign finding
Additional imaging or prior films are needed
The finding is highly suggestive of malignancy
questions.detail: Category 0 is a preliminary assessment used only in screening when a final assessment cannot be made without further workup.

questions.question: Which BI-RADS category is assigned to a finding that is described but is 'definitely benign,' such as a simple cyst or vascular calcifications?
questions.detail: Category 2 indicates a normal periodic screening recommendation with no additional follow-up required for that specific finding.

questions.question: 'Category 1' in the BI-RADS lexicon is defined as:
questions.detail: BI-RADS 1 means the breasts are symmetrical and no masses, architectural distortions, or suspicious calcifications are present.

questions.question: Diagnostic mammography reports MUST conclude with a final assessment from which range?
questions.detail: Category 0 is inappropriate for diagnostic exams; a definitive assessment (1–6) must be assigned after completion of the workup.

questions.question: A BI-RADS 6 assessment is reserved for:
choices: Biopsy-proven malignancy prior to definitive therapy
questions.detail: This category is used for patients with known cancer undergoing imaging for treatment planning or monitoring.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four standardized breast density categories in BI-RADS?
questions.detail: The standardized categories are A (fatty), B (scattered), C (heterogeneously dense), and D (extremely dense).
